title: Utah Supreme Court Rules of Professional Practice 1-701 and 1-704: Office of Legal Services Innovation
author: Utah Supreme Court

dom.t: Regulatory sandboxes: Conditional entry tests consumer risk

mo.t: Ownership reform: Investment openings may miss justice needs
Regulatory sandboxes: Conditional entry tests consumer risk
Supervised AI: Verification may consume efficiency gains

kp.k: Pilot sandbox regulates nontraditional legal services and providers
kp.d: Rule 1-701, effective November 1, 2024, establishes the institutional purpose of the Office of Legal Services Innovation and its advisory committee: assisting Supreme Court oversight of nontraditional providers and services through a pilot regulatory sandbox. The text provides a regulatory framework, not findings about its effects, and does not specifically discuss AI.
qs: The Supreme Court created the Office of Legal Services Innovation and the Legal Services Innovation Committee to assist the Supreme Court in overseeing and regulating nontraditional legal services providers and the delivery of nontraditional legal services through a pilot legal regulatory sandbox.

kp.k: Bar-housed office operates under Supreme Court policies
kp.d: The Office operates the sandbox from within the Utah State Bar under Supreme Court policies, while the Committee advises the Court through policy-based recommendations. The rule assigns distinct operational and advisory responsibilities.
qs: The Office of Legal Services Innovation will be housed at the Utah State Bar and is responsible for operating the legal regulatory sandbox in accordance with the policies adopted by the Supreme Court.
The Office of Legal Services Innovation Committee is a Supreme Court advisory committee that makes policy-based recommendations for action by the Court.

kp.k: Sandbox entry requires review and recommended Court approval
kp.d: Rule 1-704 assigns the Committee responsibility for assessing whether applicants satisfy sandbox admission requirements. It may seek additional information, deny applications, or recommend Supreme Court approval; the text does not specify the substantive admission requirements.
qs: The Committee reviews entity applications and assesses whether the entity has met the requirements for admission to the Sandbox.
The Committee may require the applicant to provide additional information, may deny an application, or may recommend that the Supreme Court approve the application.

kp.k: Policy mandate prioritizes access, quality, affordability, and competition
kp.d: The Committee must develop and recommend policies intended to support consumer access to an innovative, affordable, competitive and high-quality legal services market. This is a stated regulatory objective, not evidence that the sandbox has achieved those outcomes.
qs: The Committee is responsible for developing and recommending policies to the Supreme Court to ensure that consumers have access to a well-developed, high-quality, innovative, affordable, and competitive market for legal services.

kp.k: Consumer harm monitoring combines data, complaints, and assessments
kp.d: The Committee's oversight mandate includes monitoring entity data, consumer complaints, pre-launch assessments and audits for evidence of consumer harm, with regular reporting to the Supreme Court. No monitoring results or measured harm rates are supplied.
qs: The Committee monitors entity data, consumer complaints, and the results of pre-launch assessments and audits for evidence of consumer harm.
The Committee reports its findings and recommendations to the Supreme Court on a regular basis.

kp.k: Authorization remains subject to suspension or termination
kp.d: The Committee may suspend or terminate a sandbox entity's authorization under the Innovation Office Manual. The rule differentiates reinstatement eligibility: suspended entities may apply at any time through an affidavit, whereas terminated entities must wait three years from termination.
qs: The Committee may suspend or terminate any entity's authorization as governed by the Innovation Office Manual.
An entity may apply for reinstatement at any time by submitting an affidavit for reinstatement.
A previously terminated entity may apply for reinstatement after three years from the termination date.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: The Utah Supreme Court rules contain no explicit claim or prediction about AI. They establish oversight of nontraditional legal services through a pilot regulatory sandbox and state a legal-market policy objective.
pts.d: The source assigns operation of the sandbox to the Office of Legal Services Innovation and policy recommendations and oversight responsibilities to the Committee. Its objective of an innovative, affordable, competitive legal-services market is a regulatory goal, not a finding that AI or the sandbox has produced those outcomes. The text does not identify AI providers or specify AI uses.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source is an authoritative statement of regulatory responsibilities, not empirical evidence of AI's effects.
pts.d: Rules 1-701 and 1-704 provide the authority for the institutional arrangements described. They prescribe monitoring of entity data, complaints, assessments, and audits for consumer harm, but report no results, measured benefits, or AI-specific evidence.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: Both rules take effect November 1, 2024; participation occurs within a pilot sandbox subject to admission and continuing oversight.
pts.d: The text offers no forecast horizon for AI adoption or market transformation and gives no pilot end date. The Committee reviews admission requirements and may deny applications or recommend Supreme Court approval. Entity authorization may be suspended or terminated under the Innovation Office Manual. Suspended entities may apply for reinstatement at any time by affidavit; terminated entities must wait three years.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The rules affect nontraditional legal-services providers, consumers, and the institutions administering Utah's sandbox.
pts.d: Applicant and participating entities face admission review, monitoring, and potential disciplinary action, with reconsideration and appeal procedures. Consumers are the intended beneficiaries of the stated market-access objective and consumer-harm monitoring. The Office operates the sandbox at the Utah State Bar; the Committee advises and reports to the Supreme Court. The source does not identify effects on particular lawyer roles, staffing structures, client segments, or AI vendors.
